summaries:
I reviewed 122 type-B variants (round 1) against the card texts in slots.json. m746 (Teeth Whitening) has no B variant in this batch, so it needs one. I found no hard HWG violations: no nudity, blood, before/after shots, readable text or desk-doctor scenes. The main problem is sameness. The old banned defaults have been replaced by a new set of recurring templates and characters.

Main clusters, with the member kept in each:
(1) A nurse tucks a blanket over the knees of a patient in a recliner, often laughing: m887, m890, m918, m960, m894, m930, m973, m910, m938. Keep m903.
(2) Staff hand a patient water or tea: m913, m921, m902, m910, m863, m962. Keep m971 and m752.
(3) A face close-up where only a staff member's hand appears, usually dark-skinned, touching the face, neck or shoulder: m872, m967, m920, m914, m922, m955, m962. Keep m967 and m914.
(4) A practitioner explains by touching their own cheek or jaw: m869, m874, m868. Keep m868.
(5) Neck ultrasound appears three times: m911, m935, m955. Keep m935.
(6) On the hair cards, a practitioner stands behind a seated patient parting or lifting the hair, or combing it back: m976, m977, m978, m764. Keep m977 and m764.
(7) Recovery or first-step walks: m864 is a near-copy of m866 (terracotta arches, older couple, silver-pixie wife), m900 repeats m915 (both titled "First Steps After Surgery"), and m860 is a third walk on the plastic-surgery page.
(8) Overhead shots of a patient lying on a mat with a physio kneeling beside: m950, m957, m934.
(9) Heel-to-toe balance-beam walks: m931 and m945, with n504 as a third balance scene.
(10) Paediatric wards at evening lamplight with a sleeping child and a male nurse: m938, m943, m940, m949.
(11) Macro shots of a parent's hand on a child's hand: m946 and m948.
(12) Eleven negative-space compositions (figures small in a lower third under a bare wall) and about 11 top-down overhead shots.

Recurring characters (the owner's core complaint):
- Staff: about 11 Filipino male nurses, with an identical 50s nurse with a grey crew cut in m892 and m928; about 8 Black women in their 50s with close-cropped grey natural hair (m755, m869, m895, m904, m915, m929, m956); many shaved-head men in round glasses (m930 matches m938); an East Asian woman with a grey bob (m889, m975, m909, m950).
- Patients: an older Middle-Eastern man with swept-back silver hair and a moustache (m859, m867, m964, m965, m955); an older woman with a short silver crop or pixie (m862, m888, m963, m864, m866, m863); a woman in her 50s with short salt-and-pepper hair and hoops (m872, m898, m933, m937); Ukrainian twenty-somethings with a copper-red pixie (m886 and m893) or a shaved head and freckles (m886 and m892).
- Patient look-alikes on adjacent cards: m935 and m959; m910 and m920; m904 and m929; m885 and m936; m896 and m961; m974 and m952 (also m902).

Drift towards the banned looks: m931 and m954 (dark hair streaked with silver plus gold jewellery).

Off-topic or weak fit: m888 (shows a facial, but the card is about an IV infusion), m859, m863, m962, m753, m932, m940, n501, n504.

Smaller repeated motifs: citrus peeling (m892, m905, m940), a partner holding a coat (m969, m972, m874, m928), corduroy overshirts, framing through a half-open door (about 10), headphones (m919, m936, m970) and the "laughing with the nurse" mood.

There are 38 must-fix and 33 should-fix flags below. Each has a concrete alternative chosen so it does not land in another cluster.

I reviewed 122 type-C variants. m746 (Teeth Whitening) is in slots.json but has no C variant in this batch. In the flags, code is the card code, type is always "C" (the variant type), and the problem text starts with the issue category.

Main finding: C variants are much more repetitive across cards than A, B and D are meant to be.

In total I flagged 46 must-fix and 30 should-fix. Each flag names the keeper it duplicates and gives a concrete new direction. The replacements are spread across fresh settings so they don't form new clusters: chairlift, roller rink, ice rink, pottery class, beekeeping, barbershop, palm house, campfire, basketball court, table tennis, badminton, fireflies, relay baton, kayak, playground net, snowball, garden pump, rope swing, vineyard, mountain-bike rest, and a summit profile.

I reviewed all 122 type-D variants and flagged 57: 40 must-fix and 17 should-fix. Nearly all are sameness problems; I found no banned default looks and no hard health-advertising (HWG) violations.

**Repeated subjects**
- **Microscope with a gloved hand:** 9 variants. Kept m894, m977 and m897. Flagged m886, m903, m925, m934, m959 and m935. m925 and m959 are near-identical.
- **Staff smoothing a sheet or towel on an empty table, couch or chair:** about 11 variants.
  - Aesthetic treatment rooms: kept m872; flagged m873 and m869.
  - Scanner tables: flagged m902 and m945.
- **Dental-lab technician at the bench:** 4 on the Dental page. Kept m971 and m968; flagged m743 and m975.
- **IV stand or drip chamber:** 4 variants. Kept m885; flagged m890 and m892 (must-fix) and m904 (should-fix).
- **Small vial held up to the light, or a row of vials:** flagged m893 and m920 (must-fix) and m980 (should-fix).
- **Sapling tied to a stake:** 3 variants. Kept m974; flagged m908 and m952.
- **Clay heads and clay vessels:** 5–6 variants. Kept m859 and m874; flagged m967 and m954 (must-fix) and m972 (should-fix).
- **Exact pairs where I kept one and flagged the other:**
  - Scrub sink, both titled "Scrubbing In, Rain Outside": flagged both m862 and m868; kept m915.
  - Hospital facade: kept m962, flagged m861.
  - Spiral staircase: kept m865, flagged m913.
  - Porthole door: kept m948; flagged m973 and m943.
  - Loom: kept m887, flagged m891.
  - Centrifuge: kept m978, flagged m965.
  - Liquid-nitrogen vapour: kept m960, flagged m939.
  - Petri dishes: kept m921, flagged m942.
  - Tissue-typing lab: kept m900, flagged m924.
  - Looped scope on cloth: kept m907, flagged m961.
  - Instruments laid out on a drape: kept m950, flagged m911.
  - Case-conference room: kept m916, flagged m905.
  - Thermoplastic splint: kept m947, flagged m896.
  - Colonnade: kept m958, flagged n501.
  - Navy-and-walnut fabric work: kept m864, flagged m860.
  - Seedlings in a soil tray: kept m752, flagged m764.
  - Dental microscope over an empty chair: kept m899, flagged m970.

**Weak topic fit (a layperson would not link the image to the card)**
- m861, m962, m913, m917, m886, m920, m941, m944, m958, m926 and m973. Some are covered above as duplicates.

**AI and text risks (should-fix)**
- Signage in the emergency corridor (m910).
- Screens with interface text: analyser touchscreens (m912), the conference-room wall screen (m916) and a 3D printer display (m898).
- Labels on archived slides (m929).
- Calligraphy or a seal stamp appearing in ink brush strokes (m754).
- Malformed bones and L/R markers in the hand X-ray (m940).
- A floating hand on the stair rail (m865).

**Banned looks**
- None reproduced. The masked surgeon silhouette in m868 edges toward the banned masked-doctor look; its fix removes it.

Palettes rotate evenly, so palette repeats are not a problem on their own. The trouble is pairs on the same page that also share a subject, such as m860 and m864 (both navy and walnut, both stretching fabric over wood). Two overused default devices: the three-quarter view from behind over the shoulder (about 11 variants) and walking away from the camera down a corridor (m910, m923, m958, n501). Every flag gives a concrete, distinct new direction.
